'''Imai Nogiku''' (今井 野菊, August 14, 1900 – 1982) was a Japanese local historian and poet. Her real name was '''Imai Sumie''' (今井 すみ江).<ref name="imaisuwa">Imai Nogiku, ''Suwa Monogatari'' (諏訪物語), Kokusho Kankōkai, 1975, p. 227.</ref>

== Early life and career ==
Born in [[Miyagawa Village, Suwa District, Nagano Prefecture]], now part of [[Chino, Nagano]], Imai attended Suwa Girls' High School (now [[Nagano Prefecture Suwa Futaba High School]]). While in her first year, she joined the literary magazine [[Araragi (magazine)|Araragi]], studying under [[Shimaki Akahiko|Akahiko Shimagi]] and [[Moriyama Teisen|Teisen Moriyama]].<ref>Kitazawa Toshirō, "[https://www.city.chino.lg.jp/uploaded/attachment/14289.pdf Memorial Lecture: Akahiko and His Legacy]," Chino City, 2005, p. 11.</ref><ref name="chinocity">{{Cite web|title=Yatsugatake Literary Museum|url=https://www.city.chino.lg.jp/site/y-hakubutsukan/1643.html|website=City of Chino Official Website|access-date=October 5, 2024}}</ref>

In 1918, she graduated and became a substitute teacher at a local elementary school. The following year, she married Imai Heizaemon, a kanten (agar-agar) wholesaler.<ref name="imaisuwa"/><ref name="chinocity"/> A licensed instructor of the [[Ikenobō|Ikenobō School]], she was affectionately referred to as "the teacher of Chigamise" in her community.<ref name="suwagaku">Yamamoto Hiroko et al., ''Suwa Studies'' (諏訪学), Kokusho Kankōkai, 2018, pp. 418–420.</ref>

Following World War II, Imai dedicated herself to compiling the ''Old Miyagawa Village History'' while conducting extensive research on [[Suwa Faith|Suwa Shrine]], including the worship of [[Mishaguji]], [[Chikatō-no-Kami]], and [[Tenpaku faith|Amabe no Kami]]. Her work included field surveys and preserving local heritage.<ref name="kobuzoku">Ancient Tribes Research Association, ''Ancient Suwa and the Mishaguji Ritual State,'' Ningen Publishing, 2017, p. 308.</ref> Imai passed away in 1982.<ref name="kobuzoku"/>

=== Contributions to Suwa Faith and Mishaguji Research ===
In 1953, alarmed by the destruction of ancient Kofuns and ruins near the [[Maemiya Shrine of Suwa Taisha|Suwa Taisha Maemiya]], Imai, together with historian Hosokawa Hayato, established the ''Old Miyagawa Village History Compilation Research Association.'' Initially attracting over 50 participants, the project gradually dwindled to just Imai. Immersed in the study of Mishaguji, Imai compiled her findings into 25 booklets distributed for free to local residents.

She also conducted field research across Japan, often traveling on foot and camping outdoors. Her seminal work, ''Mishaguji Field Survey Collection,'' was included in the publication ''Ancient Suwa and the Mishaguji Ritual State.'' In addition to Mishaguji, Imai explored other facets of Suwa Faith, such as [[Chikato Worship|Chikato Faith]] and [[Tenpaku faith|Amabe Worship]].<ref name="suwagaku"/>

Her research influenced subsequent scholars, including [[Yamada Sōmoku|Munemutsu Yamada]] and the Ancient Tribes Research Association. In 1974, the association members studied directly under Imai, further developing their findings in works such as ''Ancient Suwa and the Mishaguji Ritual State'' (1975) and ''The Origins and Development of Suwa Faith'' (1978).<ref name="suwagaku"/>

== Selected Poems ==
* "While rinsing rice, clear water flows / revealing white roots / and sprouting parsley" (1929)<ref name="tankashuu">Obi Sagyu (ed.), ''Suwa Tanka Collection,'' Nanshin Nichinichi Shinbunsha, 1929, p. 181.</ref>
* "Kites circle the gentle waves of spring's Sumida River, silent in flight" (1929)<ref name="tankashuu"/>
* "We converse, brushing tobacco ash from palms / crouched in the narrow mountain path" (1929)<ref>''Araragi,'' Vol. 22, No. 12, 1929, p. 165.</ref>
* "Wordlessly, I watch my son leave for war / tears fall as I prepare tea" (1944)<ref>''Araragi,'' Vol. 37, No. 5, 1944, p. 43.</ref>

== Major Works ==
* ''Suwa Tanka Collection'' (1929)
* ''Clouds on the Horizon'' (1942, under the name Imai Sumie)<ref>''Nagano Prefectural Library General Catalog,'' 1977, p. 386.</ref>
* ''The Tales of Suwa'' (1960)
* ''Mishaguji Field Survey Collection'' (1975, included in ''Ancient Suwa and the Mishaguji Ritual State'')
